Extended Station Redundancy Analysis¶

Companion report to the main Network Analysis.

This notebook extends the temperature-only redundancy result in the main report with five additional perspectives:

  1. Multivariate redundancy — correlation, clustering, and scatter analysis across the four FWI core inputs (temperature, RH, wind, rain) plus all six FWI output codes (FFMC, DMC, DC, ISI, BUI, FWI).
  2. Extreme-event correlation — agreement between stations during 95th/99th percentile conditions and fire-weather days (FWI ≥ 15), where consistency matters most.
  3. Leave-one-out (LOO) degradation — for each station, recompute the network's FWI chain with that station's contributions to cross-station imputation removed; measure how much the remaining stations' values change. A station whose removal causes large LOO degradation is load-bearing for the network and should not be decommissioned.
  4. Block-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (10 000 iterations, 24-hour blocks) on every pairwise correlation reported in the main analysis.
  5. Partial correlation controlling for Stanhope (residualisation) to distinguish direct station-to-station relationships from both-being-driven-by-regional-weather relationships.

How this report is rendered. The figures shown below were generated during the original run of this notebook (commit e638648, 2026-04-05) and have been recovered from git history. The notebook code is preserved as-is so the analysis can be re-executed against fresh data; the recovered figures are embedded directly into each cell so this report is readable without re-running it.

Audience: technical reviewers and anyone who wants the multivariate / LOO evidence behind the main report's removal recommendation.

Station Redundancy Analysis¶

Pairwise correlation, PCA, hierarchical clustering, and stanhope benchmarking across all 6 PEINP/ECCC stations for four core meteorological variables.

Stations: cavendish, greenwich, north_rustico, stanhope (ECCC), stanley_bridge, tracadie

Loaded 152489 rows across 6 stations
Date range: 2023-04-01 -> 2026-03-24

  Air Temperature: 26113 hours, PC1=0.963

  Relative Humidity: 26113 hours, PC1=0.793

  Wind Speed: 26113 hours, PC1=0.709

  Precipitation: 26113 hours, PC1=0.547
Done.

1. Correlation Heatmaps¶

Pairwise Pearson correlation for each variable across all 6 stations. Values close to 1.0 indicate redundant signals; values < 0.7 indicate independent information.

2. Hierarchical Clustering Dendrograms¶

Agglomerative clustering (average linkage) on distance = 1 - r. Stations that merge early are the most redundant.

3. Temperature Scatter - The Tight Cluster¶

Cavendish, north rustico, and tracadie have pairwise r >= 0.994 for temperature. These scatter plots show how tightly coupled they are.

4. Temperature Scatter - All Stations vs Stanhope¶

Every PEINP station plotted against the ECCC stanhope reference.

5. Stanhope Benchmark - Mean Absolute Difference¶

How far each station deviates from stanhope on average, per variable.

6. Summary: Recommendation Matrix¶

Keep/remove/defer recommendation per station per variable, with risk band from uncertainty quantification.

9. Partial Correlation - Controlling for Stanhope¶

Strips out the shared regional weather signal by conditioning on stanhope (the ECCC reference). If partial r collapses, stations merely share an airmass; if it stays high, they are genuinely locally redundant.

10. Extreme Event Correlation¶

Stations agree on calm days - the real question is whether they agree when conditions are dangerous. Correlation is computed only on hours where either station exceeds the 95th or 99th percentile. FWI fire-weather days (FWI >= 15, FWI >= 25) are analysed separately.

11. FWI-Component Redundancy¶

Run the full correlation / PCA / clustering suite on the six FWI outputs (FFMC, DMC, DC, ISI, BUI, FWI) instead of raw meteorological inputs. DC and DMC are daily-integrated (slow response) and should cluster tightly; FFMC is hourly (fast response) and may diverge more.

  FFMC: 26093 hours, PC1=0.854
  DMC : 26110 hours, PC1=0.932
  DC  : 26110 hours, PC1=0.967

  ISI : 26090 hours, PC1=0.661
  BUI : 26090 hours, PC1=0.943
  FWI : 26090 hours, PC1=0.872
FWI component analysis complete.

12. Leave-One-Out FWI Degradation¶

The most direct redundancy test: identify which rows in each station's hourly data were cross-station imputed from a given donor, then measure how much FWI changes when that donor is removed. Stations whose removal causes < 1 FWI point MAE across the network are redundant.
